statement.p: Which of the following differential equations are separable? (Select all that apply.)
Now consider the following equation. \int f'(x) \, dx = \int x \, dx
Which of the following functions f(x) satisfy this equation? (Select all that apply.)

static.solution:
g(y) \frac{dy}{dt} = h(t). For example, (1) \frac{dy}{dt} = t+1, \left( \frac{1}{y} \right) \frac{dy}{dt} = t-1, and \left( \frac{1}{y} \right) \frac{dy}{dt} = -3 are all separable. The equation \frac{dy}{dt} = t^2 - y^2 is not separable, however, because the right-hand side cannot be factored into a product of a function of y and a function of t.
For the second part, note that a solution must be an antiderivative of x.
